    AI Overview
    Artemis II, NASA's first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years, took four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon and safely back, splashing down on April 10, 2026. The crew tested the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space, set a human distance record from Earth, and paved the way for future lunar landings. 
    Key Mission Accomplishments & Actions: 
    • Crewed Lunar Flyby: NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen flew around the Moon, reaching the far side.
    • Distance Record: The crew set a new record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth by humans, reaching 252,756 miles (406,771 km) on April 6, 2026.
    • Historic Milestones: Victor Glover became the first person of color, Christina Koch the first woman, and Jeremy Hansen the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
    • System Testing: Astronauts performed manual flying tests, evaluated life support systems, and tested the spacecraft's communication systems and new, improved toilet system.
    • Observations & Science: The crew observed the Moon’s surface, taking photos and notes to help determine geological composition.
    • Safe Return: The mission concluded with a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California after a high-speed, high-temperature reentry.

    What did Artemis II do?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Artemis II successfully completed a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon in April 2026, traveling farther than any human in history (over 252,000 miles) to test the Orion spacecraft's systems. The four-person crew validated life-support systems, conducted deep-space maneuvers, and documented lunar surface conditions ahead of future landing missions. 
    Key Achievements of the Mission: 
    • Deep Space Travel: The mission was the first crewed flight to leave Earth's orbit since 1972, with astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen traveling beyond the Moon.
    • System Testing: The crew tested Orion's environmental control systems, communications, and navigation in deep space, ensuring it is safe for future crewed landings.
    • Scientific Observations: Astronauts studied the lunar surface, documenting impact craters, lava flows, and reporting six meteoroid impact flashes.
    • Unique Observations: The crew observed a unique, hour-long solar eclipse from space, seeing the Sun's corona from beyond the Moon's far side.
    • Operational Success: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket performed within specifications, with the spacecraft executing a "flawless" translunar injection burn. 
    The crew, including Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, successfully completed their objectives and prepared for a planned splashdown off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026.
